_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Hardware Bill of Materials Requirements
summary: Requires suppliers to provide a Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM) cataloging hardware components to support Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) practices.
use_relationship:
This Data Item Description (DID) is designated to ensure that suppliers and vendors are actively engaged in maintaining and improving Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (C-SCRM) practices. The DID mandates the creation and provision of a comprehensive Hardware Bill of Materials (HBOM). It provides a standardized and systematic methodology for cataloging hardware components within embedded and connected devices to facilitate better understanding and management of potential cybersecurity risks.

a. The HBOM provided must be a representation of the production release manufacturing bill of materials, or "as-built" BOM representing the components that were actually used in the production of the product. These should include (where applicable)

(1) Configurable BOM (CBOM) - These BOMs describe multiple options in the manufacturing process driven by selection of options for unique models in a product family. The supplier must provide all iterations of the BOM that are relevant for the "as-built" models procured by the customer.

(2) BOM Variant - These BOMs describe multiple options in the manufacturing process used for the same model of a product. For instance, one server may use network adapter cards from multiple vendors with the same form, fit and function. If BOM variants are used for this purpose, the supplier must provide all of the relevant BOM variants for the "as-built" models procured by the customer.

(3) Manufacturing Deviations - Any exceptions to approved or "as-built" manufacturing that have been applied. These are temporary exceptions to documented manufacturing procedure or process that are put in place until a permanent change can be made. For instance, a component may have been specified with a tighter tolerance than actually needed (1% instead of 5%) for form, fit, and function. A deviation can be written to allow use of 5% parts for a specified period of time while a change order is written to replace the 1% parts.

b. Unless otherwise specified hardware BOM type should not include:

(1) Engineering BOM (EBOM) - Used in the design of the product, but may not be an accurate representation of the manufactured product. This would only be appropriate in the prototype phase of a project.

c. The word "item" is used throughout the document to refer to hardware components of the system.

d. This DID contain the format, content, and intended use information for the data product resulting from the work task described in the solicitation.

e. This DID should be tailored in the Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) to include the necessary field categories from Table 1.

preparation_instructions.title: Format
preparation_instructions.content: The C-SCRM HBOM shall be submitted in English and machine-readable format to ensure interoperability and automation support.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The data provided in the HBOM must adhere to the standards and specifications set forth in this document. As stipulated by the contract, the data must encompass the information outlined in the Field Name and Description columns detailed in Table 1. Fields for which data is not available shall be left blank. Vendors are required to provide an HBOM breakdown as shown in Figure 1, demonstrating a hierarchical decomposition of the product.
